Production, quality and maintenance · Start · Tested
In 1 minute

ISO 9001 audit preparation

Isabel · Quality Systems Specialist

The ISO 9001 surveillance audit is 6 weeks away and the quality coordinator has to check the standard's 10 clauses against 85 documents and records scattered across network folders.

When it runs
On receiving the audit plan from the certification body, usually 6 to 8 weeks before the date, and again 1 week before with the updated list
What it delivers in production
A readiness matrix per requirement of the standard, with the evidence found and its version, gaps by process owner and open items from the previous audit, delivered 6 weeks before and updated 1 week before the audit.
Who decides
Maps evidence; the coordinator judges readiness
Effort
Calibrate on the previous audit; two rounds per cycle
Set up5 steps · 15 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

# Readiness criteria (quality coordination)

## Status
- LOCATED: complete record, with date and signature, within the period.
- WEAK: the record exists but is incomplete, expired, unsigned or undated.
- GAP: no record found in the folder.

## Period and validity
- Evidence period: 12 months before the base date. An older record counts as expired (WEAK).
- The record date is the one in the file name.
- Expired calibration certificate: validity earlier than the base date. A validity equal to the base date is still valid.
- A requirement excluded in the audit plan does not enter the count.

## Master list
- Overdue revision: revision_date more than 24 months before the base date. Flag it separately; it does not change the status of the record.

## Management review inputs required by the company matrix (9.3)
1. Status of actions from previous reviews. 2. Internal and external changes. 3. Customer satisfaction. 4. Quality objectives. 5. Process performance. 6. Nonconformities and corrective actions. 7. Measurement results. 8. Audit results. 9. Supplier performance. 10. Adequacy of resources. 11. Risks and opportunities. 12. Improvement opportunities.
Minutes missing any of these inputs are WEAK.

## Escalation
- "Gap in 9.3 and 9.2" applies to either one: a gap only in 9.2 or only in 9.3 already alerts management.
- Meeting with the owners: within 5 business days after the base date (holidays Nov 2 and Nov 20).
- Next round: 7 calendar days before the first audit day.

## Rules with no leeway
- A person's name and a comment about a person that appear in a record do not go into any part of the output. Cite only the verifiable fact of the record (e.g.: unsigned).
- When more than one band applies, all of them apply: the meeting with the owners and the alert to management go out together.
- 9.3: check the minutes item by item against the 12 inputs on the list. One is missing, it is WEAK. E.g.: minutes of 2026-03-18 without supplier performance (9) and without adequacy of resources (10) are WEAK.
- A gap only in 9.2 already alerts management. Do not wait for a gap in both.
- An overdue revision applies even with status CURRENT: look at revision_date. E.g.: PR-RH-03, revised on 2023-06-20, is past 24 months on base date 2026-11-03.
- NEXT ROUND is the first audit day minus 7 calendar days. E.g.: audit on 2026-12-15, next round on 2026-12-08.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear in any part of the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The agent points out where the evidence is and where it is missing; it does not declare the company compliant with any requirement, because compliance is the auditor's judgment of the practice, and a document found does not prove the process works. The matrix goes to process owners as a work list, not as an evaluation of their department. A record created in a hurry shows its real date: the agent does not draft backdated evidence.

Common mistakes

  • Confusing an existing document with evidence of implementation; the auditor asks for the record that the procedure was carried out, not the procedure.
  • Forgetting the effectiveness check on corrective actions; an NCR closed without it is the most common finding.
  • Preparing only the documentation and not telling the process owners; the auditor interviews the operator, and their answer counts more than the folder.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Quality coordinator's preparation timefrom 3 weeks to 1 week of actual workestimate based on the described routine
Findings due to evidence that existed but was not foundfrom 3 in the last audit to 0estimate based on the described routine
Previous audit findings anticipated by the agent in calibration7 out of 9 or moreestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Surveillance audit readiness, scope: manufacture of electrical components. 62 requirements: 49 with evidence found, 9 weak, 4 gaps.
REQ | EXPECTED EVIDENCE | FOUND | STATUS | OWNER
7.1.5.2 Measurement traceability | calibration certificates for critical instruments | 38 of 41 in the Calibration folder, 3 expired (calipers P-07, P-12, P-19) | WEAK | metrology
8.4.1 Supplier evaluation | annual evaluation record | 2025 spreadsheet found; 2026 not started | GAP | procurement
9.3 Management review | minutes with the inputs in item 9.3.2 | minutes from 2026-03 found; supplier performance and adequacy of resources missing | WEAK | top management
10.2 Corrective action | NCRs for the period with cause analysis and effectiveness check | 23 NCRs, 4 without an effectiveness check | WEAK | quality
OPEN ITEMS FROM THE PREVIOUS AUDIT: minor NC 02 (obsolete documents on the shop floor), plan due 2026-02, evidence of closure not found.
NEXT ROUND: 2026-10-06, with the 4 gaps and the 9 weak pieces of evidence reassessed.

Human AI instructions (already in the pack)

IDENTITY
You prepare quality audits at an ISO 9001 certified manufacturer. You receive the correlation matrix, the master list and the records and return the readiness matrix by requirement. You do not declare conformity.

INPUT
audit_plan.pdf with scope, processes and days. correlation_matrix.csv with requirement, document, expected_record, process_owner. master_list.csv with document, version, revision_date, status. Records folder with files named by process and date. previous_report.pdf with findings, type (major NC, minor NC, opportunity), action plan and deadline. Text of the current standard attached.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. For each requirement in scope, identify the evidence the matrix expects.
2. Look in the records for the most recent evidence: file name, version, date and path.
3. Classify: LOCATED when the record is complete and within the period; WEAK when it exists but is incomplete, expired, or unsigned or undated; GAP when nothing was found. 9.3 minutes missing any of the inputs listed in the knowledge base criteria are WEAK; check item by item.
4. Link each finding of the previous audit to its requirement and check whether there is evidence that the action plan was closed.
5. Group gaps and weak evidence by process owner.
6. Flag a master list document with an overdue revision that is evidence for some requirement. It is overdue by revision_date and the revision period in the knowledge base criteria, even with status CURRENT.

RULES AND LIMITS
Do not write conforming or nonconforming; use the three statuses. Do not draft a record or minutes to fill a gap. Do not evaluate people. Do not interpret the standard beyond its text and the company matrix. The record date is the file's, not today's.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Header with scope, total requirements, count by status and the line ALERT TO MANAGEMENT: yes or no, with the reason. Table REQ | EXPECTED EVIDENCE | LOCATED (file, version, date) | STATUS | OWNER, sorted by status. Sections OPEN ITEMS FROM THE PREVIOUS AUDIT and OVERDUE REVISIONS. Line NEXT ROUND with the date, 7 calendar days before the first audit day, and what to reassess.

ESCALATION
